attacks.claim: The agreed invariant is that devices must always be able to return to the previous firmware. The only automatic revert covers boot and self-test failure. The only other path is an OTA push of 4.7, so a 4.8 unit that boots and self-tests but cannot reach the OTA service (4.8 changes Wi-Fi reconnect behaviour) cannot be returned to 4.7. The same gap applies to units that are offline or deferred during a revert campaign, and the artifact does not say what state they are left in.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically." / "Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path" / "Halt: pause the OTA campaign (one switch); units not yet updated stay on 4.7." ABSENT: a rollback path for 4.8 units that cannot reach OTA, and a plan for offline or deferred units during revert.

attacks.claim: Away Assist infers absence from one thermostat-mounted motion sensor. Occupants who are still for 2 h in the sensor's room, or who are outside its field of view, will be set to Away during scheduled home periods, and the Away setpoints then apply. The artifact has no stillness tolerance, sensor coverage analysis, false-Away measurement, or safeguard for sleeping occupants, pets, or sensor faults.
attacks.evidence: "the thermostat's built-in motion sensor sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods, and returns to schedule on the first motion" / QA: "on → Away after 2 h no motion, back on motion | Pass". ABSENT: false-Away rate, sensor coverage limits, or a stillness-tolerance analysis.

attacks.claim: Paging does not cover the metrics that gate stage advancement. Stages advance only if HVAC fault telemetry and support contacts are not above baseline, and Away Assist anomalies are not monitored at all. Only boot reverts and offline rate page on-call, so a regression in HVAC faults, support volume, or Away transitions would not alert anyone.
attacks.evidence: "Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline." versus "advance only if ... HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline, support contacts per 1k units not above baseline"

attacks.claim: The stage gates have no defined statistics, and the cohorts are not representative of installed units. At 1% (~6,100 units) and a 0.05% boot-revert threshold, roughly 3 events are the limit, so the gate cannot detect a real regression. HVAC-fault gates have no thresholds or power analysis. Install deferral for temperature, the 02:00–05:00 window, and 14-day postponements skew the installed sample toward mild-climate homes, so the gates may miss the failures that matter most.
attacks.evidence: "1% (~6,100) | 3 days | boot-revert rate < 0.05%, HVAC fault telemetry not above 4.7 baseline, support contacts per 1k units not above baseline" / "Each stage is a random sample stratified by hardware rev and HVAC type." / "Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app." ABSENT: installed-versus-targeted counts, power analysis, or climate-stratified checks.

attacks.claim: The claim that freeze and heat protection is never interrupted is an absolute that the QA does not support. Relays are held open for about 90 s during install, and a failed install can reboot the unit three times before revert. Deferral was tested only at 5 °C, so the 7 °C and 32 °C boundaries are untested. Power loss during install is not tested.
attacks.evidence: "so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted" / "During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off)." / "Temperature deferral at 5 °C chamber test | Pass, install deferred" ABSENT: boundary tests at 7 °C and 32 °C, a power-interruption-during-install test, or worst-case outage duration for the 3-boot revert loop.

attacks.claim: Schedule consistency is handled only for edits made by a 4.7 unit. Edits from app 9.2, offline sync, or cloud-side changes may leave a stale v2 copy that diverges from v1 and is restored on re-upgrade. The re-upgrade path after a 4.7 edit is not in the QA table, and no test covers it.
attacks.evidence: "When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule." / QA: "edit on 4.8, downgrade to 4.7 via OTA, schedule present and correct" (no re-upgrade test). ABSENT: v2 invalidation for app 9.2, offline, or cloud edits.

attacks.claim: The v1 downgrade schedule is derived by an unspecified rule, and the rule decides which user setpoints survive. The 'simplified' notice tells users their schedule changed but gives no way to see or restore dropped periods. Revert also deletes Home/Away history and discards v2 schedule detail, with no restore path. The rule is untestable as written, and the data-loss behaviour is not disclosed as a user impact.
attacks.evidence: "keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors" / "The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods." / "Revert: ... schedules fall back to their v1 copy and Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)." ABSENT: distance or tie-break definition, test cases for off-anchor setpoints, and a user-visible restore path.

attacks.claim: The public energy claim (median 6% runtime reduction) rests on a 412-home trial. The artifact does not state the trial design (control group, significance, population representativeness) or that the trial firmware ran the same Away logic that ships in 4.8. Legal substantiation review is referenced but not shown in the artifact. Published before that is established, the claim is a misleading-advertising risk.
attacks.evidence: "In our 2025-26 field trial of 412 homes, Away Assist cut heating runtime by a median of 6%." / "reviewed by legal for substantiation, LGL-4472" ABSENT: control design, trial firmware and Away-logic match to 4.8, and statistical basis for the median.

attacks.claim: Auto-revert covers only boot failure and failed self-test. A unit that boots and passes self-test but has a latent HVAC or relay fault is not reverted automatically and depends on manual detection and a fleet-wide revert.
attacks.evidence: "If 4.8 fails to boot or fails its post-boot self-test 3 times, the unit reverts to 4.7 automatically."

attacks.claim: The state handling for units in active Away mode at the moment of revert is unspecified. A unit reverted during a cold night could remain on Away setpoints without a defined return-to-schedule step.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: state handling for units in active Away mode at revert; "Away Assist turns off" is the only statement.

attacks.claim: QA evidence is small relative to the 612k fleet. The HIL bench ran 72 h, the employee beta covered 1,140 homes for 3 weeks, and the Away trial covered 412 homes. These do not represent rare field failures or the mixed HVAC and rev combinations, so the employee beta's 'no increase in support contacts' is weak evidence for the public gate.
attacks.evidence: "HIL bench: ... Pass, 0 relay faults over 72 h" / "Employee beta: 1,140 homes for 3 weeks | Crash-free 99.97%, no increase in support contacts"

attacks.claim: Telemetry from units that auto-revert may be lost, so the boot-revert rate that gates stage advance could under-count failures.
attacks.evidence: "boot-revert rate < 0.05%"; ABSENT: how reverted units that fail to report telemetry are counted.

attacks.claim: Stage 4 has no duration, gate, or halt criteria, so the step from 50% to 100% moves the remaining ~306k units at once.

The OTA egress estimate assumes one download per unit and excludes retries and deferred re-attempts, so it is a lower bound. Storage for dual v1/v2 schedules fleet-wide and 7-day Home/Away retention is not costed.
attacks.evidence: "OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB via existing CDN contract, within the monthly commit." / "projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest" ABSENT: storage cost for dual schedule copies.

attacks.claim: The public timeline 'over the next two weeks' does not match the stage durations (3 + 4 + 4 days, plus an open-ended stage 4 gated on criteria), so the published expectation may be wrong.
attacks.evidence: "Rolling out over the next two weeks." versus stage durations of 3, 4 and 4 days and open-ended stage 4

attacks.claim: App 9.3 behaviour when editing a schedule on a 4.7 unit is unspecified. The artifact says the app works with both firmware versions but does not say how 8-period edits are written to a 4.7 unit.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.3 works with both 4.7 and 4.8 units; no app rollback needed." ABSENT: how 9.3 writes 8-period edits to a 4.7 unit.

attacks.claim: Accessibility checks cover the app 9.3 editor and Away Assist screens only. The 9.2 'Update the app to edit this schedule' prompt and any thermostat-side Away state are not shown as tested.
attacks.evidence: "App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text | Pass" / "App 9.2 viewing an 8-period schedule shows update prompt, no edit | Pass" (no accessibility qualifier)

attacks.claim: Release notes and the privacy notice do not disclose that reverting deletes Home/Away history, so users are not told about this data-loss effect.
attacks.evidence: "Revert: push 4.7 ... Away Assist turns off (Home/Away history is deleted)." ABSENT: user-facing disclosure of this deletion in release notes or privacy notice.
